# Y8960 PCM file

> This is an English translation of the [Japanese original](../pcmfile.md). Where the two differ, the Japanese version is authoritative.

**This document specifies two files that carry ADPCM data.** It collects the information needed to write tools on the PC side that create these files, or that read them and extract their contents.

- The file that `CALL EXPORT PCM` writes and `CALL IMPORT PCM` reads — carries the voice file settings and the contents of ADPCM memory together. From "What it carries" through "Relation to sequence data"
- The file that `CALL SAVE PCM` writes and `CALL LOAD PCM` reads — carries one voice file. "[Single voice file](#single-voice-file)"

For how to use the statements, see [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md); for the form of sequence data, see [`bytecode.md`](bytecode.md).

What this document specifies is **the byte sequence of the whole file**. The ADPCM encoding itself (how many samples one byte holds) is not part of this format — the file carries the contents of the sound chip's sample memory as is, which is the same as the MSX-AUDIO internal representation.

## What it carries

This file carries two things. **A file can also carry only one of them.**

- **Voice file settings** (hereafter "settings"). For each number, the location, length and sampling frequency
- **Contents of ADPCM memory** (hereafter "dump"). The byte sequence of the sound chip's sample memory

A **voice file** is a unit of sound called by a number 0-63, and MML `@`*n* selects this number. For each number, the settings hold where it is and how many pages it occupies, and at what rate it is played.

**A page is 256 bytes**, and all lengths and positions are in pages. ADPCM memory is **256KB = 1024 pages**.

**Only voice files placed in ADPCM memory go into the settings.** Those placed in an array variable or VRAM are not included, because they have meaning only on that machine at that time — they also cannot be played as they are (the sound chip can read only its own memory).

## Overall layout

A 9-byte header, the settings, and the dump, in that order. **The file ends with these three; there is no end marker.**

| Position | Size | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 9 | Header |
| 9 | 7×*n* | Settings. 7 bytes per entry |
| 9+7×*n* | 256×*m* | Dump. *m* pages from page 0 of ADPCM memory |

**All 2-byte values are low byte first.**

### Header (9 bytes)

| Offset | Size | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 4 | `59 38 50 43` (`"Y8PC"`) |
| 4 | 1 | Version. Currently `01` |
| 5 | 1 | Contents. bit0 is the settings, bit1 is the dump. bit2-7 are 0 |
| 6 | 1 | Number of settings entries *n* (0-64) |
| 7 | 2 | Number of dump pages *m* (0-1024) |

**The contents bits are exactly the mode passed to `CALL EXPORT PCM`.** The count for the one whose bit is not set is 0 — a settings-only file has *m* of 0, and a dump-only file has *n* of 0.

**A contents bit may be set with a count of 0.** If the settings were requested on export and there is not a single voice file in ADPCM memory, bit0 stays set and *n* is 0.

## Settings

7 bytes per entry. **The number of entries is *n* in the header.**

| Offset | Size | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | Voice file number (0-63) |
| 1 | 2 | First page in ADPCM memory |
| 3 | 2 | Number of pages |
| 5 | 2 | Sampling frequency (Hz, 1800-16000) |

**Conditions the values must meet.** The number is 0-63. The number of pages is 1 or more. First page + number of pages is 1024 or less. The frequency is 1800-16000. The number of entries is 64 or less. **If even one of them is out of range, the whole file is rejected and the settings do not change at all.**

**The order has no meaning.** On export the entries are in ascending order of number, but the reader does not require any order. **If the same number appears twice, the later one remains.** Whether regions overlap is not checked.

### Loading replaces all settings

**When settings are loaded, all 64 numbers are first emptied, and only those the file names are set.** Numbers not in the file, including those that were placed in an array variable or VRAM, end up with no settings. What the file says is not added to the existing settings; **the file's settings become the new settings as they are.**

**The first page is used as the file says.** The reader does not reassign locations — the file decides where in ADPCM memory each number lies. So the dump and the settings need to refer to the same arrangement.

### Sampling frequency

**The file holds Hz.** The sound chip holds a step relative to 49716Hz; it is converted to Hz on export and to a step on import.

**Every value in 1800-16000 is unchanged by exporting and then importing.** The rounding is chosen so that it cancels out over the round trip. A file with a value outside the range is rejected.

## Dump

**The *m* pages from page 0 of ADPCM memory, laid out as they are.** 256 bytes per page, with no separators between them.

**What is exported is from page 0 to the last page reached by a voice file placed in ADPCM memory.** If there is a gap that no number uses, that gap is also included as is — this is so that the export does not shift positions, and a page's position is directly its position in ADPCM memory. If not a single voice file is placed in ADPCM memory, *m* is 0.

**On import, *m* pages from page 0 are overwritten.** What lies beyond them does not change.

**The byte sequence is exactly the contents of the sound chip's sample memory.** The encoding is the same as the MSX-AUDIO internal representation, and this file format does not interpret the contents.

## Versions and unknown contents

- **A file whose `"Y8PC"` and version do not match is not read.** The version is 1 byte and currently `01`. If the version differs, the very form of the header may differ, and where to read the following lengths from cannot be determined
- **Only bit0 and bit1 of the contents bits are used.** The rest are set to 0 — the position of the dump is determined by 9+7×*n*, so there is no room to insert anything else there
- **A file that lacks the requested contents is not read.** A file without bit0 set when the settings were requested, or without bit1 set when the dump was requested, is rejected. Reading only one of them from a file that has both is possible
- **Anything after 9+7×*n*+256×*m* is not read**

## What is rejected

Files that `CALL IMPORT PCM` does not read, and the state left in that case.

| File | What changes |
|---|---|
| `"Y8PC"` and version do not match | Nothing changes |
| The header does not have the requested contents | Nothing changes |
| Number of entries is 65 or more, number of pages is 1025 or more | Nothing changes |
| A settings value is out of range | Nothing changes |
| Shorter than the length the header states | Overwritten up to what could be read |

**The settings are all checked before the first entry is written.** Even if an out-of-range value is encountered partway, the settings remain as they were. The dump is written page by page, so **for the dump, a file cut off partway leaves it written up to that point.**

## Limits

| | |
|---|---|
| Number of settings entries *n* | 64 |
| Number of dump pages *m* | 1024 (256KB) |
| Whole file | 262601 bytes (9 + 7×64 + 256×1024) |

File names are MSX-DOS file names: up to 8 characters for the name and 3 for the extension. **No extension is
added automatically.**

## Relation to sequence data

**ADPCM samples are not included in sequence data.** What sequence data holds is chunk `03` — a copy of the locations and frequencies of the voice files the song uses, whose contents are exactly the same 7 bytes as one settings entry in this file ([`bytecode.md`](bytecode.md)).

So **to distribute a song together with its sounds, you need two files: the sequence data and this file**. Making the arrangement the song names in chunk `03` match the arrangement that this file's settings give is the distributor's job.

## Single voice file

**The file that `CALL SAVE PCM` writes and `CALL LOAD PCM` reads.** Its form is the same as what `CALL SAVE PCM` of the MSX-AUDIO BASIC extension writes, and files written on the MSX-AUDIO side can also be read as they are.

After a 15-byte header, the contents of the voice file follow as they are. **There is no end marker.** All 2-byte values are low byte first.

| Offset | Size | Contents | Read by `LOAD PCM` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | `FE` | Read. Rejected if different |
| 1 | 2 | `0000` | Not read |
| 3 | 2 | Length×256+7. `FFFF` if the length is 256 pages or more | Not read |
| 5 | 2 | `0000` (ADPCM). `0001` for files in MSX-AUDIO PCM mode | Read. Rejected if bit0 is set |
| 7 | 2 | Length (number of pages) | Read (see below) |
| 9 | 2 | Sampling frequency (Hz) | Read. Rejected if outside 1800-16000 |
| 11 | 4 | `00 00 00 00` | Not read |
| 15 | | Voice file contents | |

**The first 7 bytes are laid out like a `BSAVE` header** (identifier `FE`, start address, end address, execution address). It takes the form of the remaining bytes placed from start address 0.
**Offset 5 corresponds to the position of the execution address.**

**The 4 bytes from offset 11 are `00 80 7F 00` in files in MSX-AUDIO PCM mode.** They are 0 in ADPCM files.

### How much is loaded

The amount `LOAD PCM` reads is determined by the location of the destination voice file.

| Location | Amount read | When the contents fall short of the length (offset 7) |
|---|---|---|
| ADPCM memory, VRAM | The shorter of the voice file's length and offset 7 | Rejected (`Input past end`). The pages that could be read have been overwritten |
| Array variable | Up to the end of the file, without looking at offset 7. Cut off at the size of the array | Not rejected. The rest of the array is left as is |

**Loading does not change the voice file's length or location.** Only the sampling frequency changes, and it is overwritten after the contents have been read.
